data: Closest spacecraft to the Sun ever flown (9.86 R☉)
Added with /fly mission JSON (#341 batch 4 — Sun-skirter pair). 11.43-cm carbon-carbon Thermal Protection System sustains 1,377 °C at perihelion.
Parker Solar Probe — NASA NSSDCA (bus 3 m, TPS 2.3 m diameter)
Closest spacecraft to the Sun ever flown

NASA's Sun-grazing mission. Launched 2018-08-12 on a Delta IV Heavy + Star 48BV stack at one of the highest C3 values ever flown (154 km²/s²; only New Horizons' was higher). Seven Venus gravity assists over six years walked perihelion in from 0.16 AU (P1) to 0.046 AU (P22, 2024-12-24) — 9.86 solar radii, 6.1 million km from the Sun's surface. At P8 (2021-04-28) Parker dipped below the Alfvén critical surface — the first spacecraft to enter the Sun's corona. Peak speed at perihelion: 192.22 km/s, the fastest human-made object ever.
Closest spacecraft to the Sun ever flown (6.1 M km, 9.86 R☉); first spacecraft to enter the solar corona (2021-04-28); fastest human-made object (~191 km/s)
